details:
LunaBase is an interactive lunar exploration simulation developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge.

The project places players in the role of an astronaut conducting an Extravehicular Activity (EVA) from a lunar habitat. Players receive mission authorization, follow airlock safety procedures, manage spacesuit resources, explore the lunar surface, collect scientific samples, and return to the habitat for mission debriefing.

LunaBase introduces important lunar exploration concepts through interactive gameplay rather than relying exclusively on traditional explanations. Its simplified systems represent lunar gravity, radiation exposure, life-support monitoring, habitat power, communication limitations, and astronaut safety procedures.

The simulation includes a walkable habitat, interactive crew members, airlock controls, survival telemetry, environmental events, and a mission-success system. These features create an interconnected experience in which exploration and safety procedures influence mission progression.

The project was developed using Godot Engine 4.7.2 and GDScript. AI tools assisted with development, including coding, debugging, and documentation. The project was designed with performance limitations in mind, using the Godot Compatibility renderer.

LunaBase is an educational prototype intended to encourage curiosity about lunar exploration, astronaut training, engineering systems, and scientific discovery. Its numerical values and several operational systems are simplified gameplay assumptions rather than validated NASA mission specifications.
